chunks: Hammad narrated from Abu Kahmas, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
He was asked about the person who faints (loses consciousness): does he make up what he missed of the prayer? He said, 'As for me, my children, and my family, we do that.'

key_terms.الْمَغْمَى عَلَيْهِ: The person who faints or loses consciousness
key_terms.يَقْضِي: He makes up / performs the missed obligation

ai.seo_question: Does a person who faints need to make up their missed prayers?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the principle of *qada* (making up) for missed prayers during unconsciousness by citing his own practice and that of his family, thereby providing a practical precedent for the general ruling. This narration is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it clarifies that while the obligatory prayer is not missed during the state of *ghaybah* (unconsciousness), the duty to repay it remains, distinguishing it from the ruling for sleep or minor illness. The Imam's reference to his household underscores the continuity of this practice within the Ahl al-Bayt, reinforcing its authenticity and applicability to the faithful.
